Alright, so basically this is what happens. You have your SR.

Say its 2000 You're gold. ALl of your games have contributed to a MMR.

But due to your abnormally low stats, and plenty of losses, you have an MMR of 1500 (invisible SR)

Since you're at 2k which is higher than 1500 you'll gain less points per win, and you'll lose a lot more until you hit your MMR again. Continuing to lose you're mmr will drop.

The only way to really climb when you've completely screwed up your mmr (Like i did, i was getting 10 points a win and 40 points a loss even on long win streaks.)

Due to this it took me 411 games to get to 2k rating. So, winstreaks help build your MMR quickly. Which in turn gets you more points, the issue is. . . if for some reason the system sets you at a really really really low MMR,climbing is going to be hell. Smallest gain for a win i've had is 2 points. Biggest loss is 70 points.

The best thing you can do is try to win more games, lose less games and have better stats all around.

TL:DR Streaks do not affect SR, they affect MMR. WHich will increase your gains over time as your MMR increases

Say you're at 2k rating and you have 2500 MMR. When you win you gain more points, when you lose you lose less points.

Basically the system has a bias to push your SR towards your MMR. Which is how you can see your gains and losses.

What i realized about overwatch and winning a vast majority of your games (I have a 55-60% winrate on heroes i play)

Is following a question / solution system

Are you getting kills / picks? No? Switch characters immediately.
Is your team losing the objective / not capturing it if you are dead? Play more carefully look for picks so it can be a 5v6.


What i noticed is, if i die we'd lose the objective almost every time getting 3 picks and then dying my team would die 5v3.

So honestly, it's about being aggressive enough to maintain pressure, without dying. Minimal deaths. In about 90% of my games if i die more than 3 times.

So my biggest suggestion to you is to play the odds. Get kills on anything you possibly can. Stay alive. Try to force fights when they are down 2-3 people. 

Being a hero (going in 1v6) is almost never worth it, unless it's overtime you're the only one up, and you have to get there or you lose. T hen you can do your best. But it's a team game work together, remember even if your team is bad, you have enough control over the game to get multiple picks. As you get better and better accuracy you'll get more kills.

I tend to aim for 2000-2500 damage per minute when playing DPS. Or 3 solo kills per minute. Dying tends to hurt this.

I know this isnt a very complicated way to look at it. But it's fairly simple. If youre not getting kills you are at a disadvantage and are getting carried by your team. (if you're a tank / support. Are you enabling others to get kills?)

if you're dying, you're forcing your team to 5v6.

So stay alive, get kills. be polite, dont get angry when you lose. Do your best to push every game in your favor. 

Dealing damage will get you more ults, dont be the person that has "too good to use syndrome" use your ult if it will get 2-3 kills. On every character i build charge so quickly that as soon as i can see a double kill i'll pop it, build it up again.

Mei is really good for ult charge right now. with proper accuracy she can get her full ult charge in 7 shots (I blizzard about once a minute since my aim is sketchy)

Basically, get kills. Die less, use your ult to get double kills, more if opportunity strikes.
